podcast.body: Andy Kim considered this to be the best song of his life. Despite his strong belief in the song, it took a year and a half to get radio play, requiring him to self-finance its release and create his own record label, Ice Records, as he only had enough money for one song (Side B of the 45 was an instrumental of the track). His perseverance paid off when it became a number one hit. Released in June 1974, it remained on the Hot 100 throughout the summer before finally reaching number one. Kim intentionally avoided a guitar or drum solo, opting instead for a "Stevie Wonderish" keyboard solo near the end of the song, performed by his keyboard player. "His perseverance paid off because he not only had recorded the best song of his life he had a number one hit."
